title: ARIA Roles: When and How to Use Them

scenes.line1: When should you use ARIA roles?
scenes.say: Ever wondered when to use ARIA roles and attributes? Let's clear up how they help accessibility—and when to avoid them.

scenes.label: Native
scenes.sub: Use semantic HTML first, like buttons or alerts.
scenes.say: Start with native HTML elements. They already give browsers and screen readers the info they need.
ARIA roles define the purpose of custom widgets. Attributes like label, checked, and live give extra context to screen readers.
Here's a custom alert. ARIA tells assistive tech this is urgent, so users hear the error right away.

scenes.question: Should you use ARIA on a button?
scenes.right: No, native buttons are accessible by default. Use ARIA only when native HTML can't do the job.
scenes.say: Interviewers want to see you know: don't add ARIA to native elements like buttons. Only use ARIA when HTML doesn't cover accessibility.
